messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: production p99 decode latency spike detected in us-west-2 (svc: inference-stream). p95 increased from 120ms -> 420ms, p99 from 380ms -> 2.1s. Streaming stalls observed (clients reporting stalled chunks). Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/streams/latency?s=now-1h

maya: seeing same on infra dashboards, tails line up with a spike at 2026-03-15T02:04Z. A subset of hosts shows heavy page-fault counts + kernel evictions.

lee: which kernel/driver did we roll last night? TRT8 upgrade went to canary in us-west-2 at ~00:30Z, but only to a fraction. We rolled a compilepath change to decode kernels in the runtime at 23:50Z.

ana (typo) — actually typing as ana: @lee correct, the runtime compilepath patch (enable fast-kv-alloc) was on the edge fleet. Not all nodes. I can pull the rollout map.

jordan: customers: a few high-throughput orgs flagged errors, CS is getting p99 complaints. Ryan, heads-up?

ryan-cs: already got a handful of emails, flagged as sev-2 for impacted tenants. We told them engineering is looking. ETA for a mitigation?

maya: triage notes (initial):
- affected region: us-west-2 primary, small blips in us-west-1
- affected model families: decoder-heavy LLMs (long-context streaming)
- signal: elevated minor page faults and KV-cache churn + decode kernel p99 CPU time spikes on a subset of nodes
- likely change window: 23:45-00:45Z last night (compilepath + trt8 canary)

lee: running a quick grep on recent deploys:
```
$ git log --oneline -n 5 runtime/compilepath
f9c3d4e enable-fast-kv-alloc
b2a7c2d conda update nvcc
14a8d0e trt8 bump
```
Pattern fits. I suspect the compilepath fast-kv-alloc interacts poorly with our paging heuristic under heavy streaming load.

ana (ana): I can roll back the compilepath flag on canary to baseline. Propose: immediate rollforward -> rollback on the canary group, then monitor p99 for 2x windows. If good, schedule broader rollback.

maya: suggested mitigation order:
1) Pause new deployments to runtime in us-* (deployment-lock).
2) Roll back compilepath flag on canary nodes (lee/ana).
3) If canary rollback improves p99 by >40% within 10m, expand rollback to all affected pools.
4) As fallback, route high-SLO tenants to dedicated capacity (if available) or trigger a regional fallback to us-east-1.

lee: starting canary rollback now. Command I'm running:
```
$ infractl rollout --service runtime --tag f9c3d4e --target canary --action rollback
```
I'll post results.

(oncall-bot): Deployment action recorded: rollout rollback initiated by lee at 4890012502. See: https://deploys.redwood/runtime/rollouts/4821

maya: FYI a small subset of nodes still showing high residual page faults post-rollback — could be warmed state or kernel-level issue. Need a short window to let caches stabilize (~5-10m).

lee: canary rollback finished at 4890012570. Monitoring.

maya: initial numbers: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 720ms (within 6m). p95 down to ~260ms. Good sign but still above normal.

sam-devex: copying in a snippet customers will see in status page — short note: "We are investigating increased latency for streaming generation in us-west-2; mitigation in progress." Want to avoid overpromising.

ryan-cs: OK sending to impacted tenants now. Will update when we see consistent improvement.

ana (ana): preparing staged rollback to affected pools (non-canary) but will throttle to avoid capacity churn. Plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 20m.

lee: note: TRT8 canary was also present but at <5% traffic. I don't think it is primary, but we should keep it pinned until we finish rollback verification.

maya: two parallel investigations: runtime compilepath rollback is improving latency; kernel-level paging is still suspicious on older kernels. I'm asking infra to surface kernel package versions on affected hosts.

lee: infra response: affected hosts mostly running kernel 5.15.93-custom and an older glibc variant. There's a small overlap with a driver shim from last month.

maya: hypothesis: compilepath allocation changes increased working set pressure for streaming KV caches which triggered more frequent page reclamation on older kernels -> causing long tail stalls.

jordan: any way to proactively reduce working set pressure short-term? e.g., reduce max-batch-size or shrink kv cache TTL? Could be a low-risk stopgap.

lee: yes we can toggle runtime config:
```
runtime.config.kv_cache.max_entries = 512  # from 2048
runtime.config.decode.max_batch_tokens = 512  # from 1024
```
I'll stage those on the affected pools if rollback isn't enough.

(oncall-bot): Rollout event: staged rollback to 10% of pool started by ana at 4890012801.

maya: metrics after 15m: p99 average down to ~520ms on canary and 10% pool. Page fault rates trending down but not fully stable. Customer errors decreasing.

ryan-cs: customers reporting improved latency. Still a couple of tenants seeing degraded streaming for long contexts. Marked as partial mitigation.

maya: next steps
- continue staged rollback to 100% over next 20m (ana/lee)
- infra to inventory kernel packages and correlate to hosts with lingering tail spikes (ana/infra)
- devex (sam) to draft a short status update and playbook entry for 'compilepath-paging' (include rollback steps/flags)
- CS (ryan) to follow up impacted tenants with ETA ~1h for full mitigation
- postmortem owner: assigned to maya.

ana (ana): rolling to 30% -> 60% now.

lee: toggled kv_cache.max_entries to 512 on the 60% pool as a precaution. Monitor shows slight further drop in p99.

maya: good. if rollback + kv tuning stabilizes to p99 <350ms we can close incident as mitigated and open a follow-up for the kernel interaction investigation.

jordan: please escalate to infra security if kernel packages diverge widely; could be a release process gap.

ryan-cs: update sent to customers: "We've rolled back a runtime compilepath change and applied temporary config changes; most tenants see improved latency. Engineering continues to monitor; we'll follow up in 1 hour with final status."

(oncall-bot): Incident: mitigation_in_progress -> partial_mitigation at 4890014220.

maya: logging this as a mitigation handoff. I'll create a short timeline and collect logs + perf traces (perf, vmstat, dmesg) for postmortem. If anything regresses we re-open.

lee: thanks all — will continue rollout to remaining pools. If we get a regression on rollback revert, I'll call for cross-team pager.

sam-devex: I'll add the new runbook steps under /runbooks/compilepath-paging.md and link to the deployment commands used.

ryan-cs: I'll notify the affected customers the incident is in partial mitigation and we'll send final update when p99 stays <350ms for 30m.

maya: closing live coordination thread for now — keeping thread open for any regressions. Great job on quick rollback and config pivots. :tada:
